findings.message: Backtracking is required for the best endings. 'pick-the-lock' (threshold) needs both lock-pick (only from shop-pick) and flood-stamp (only from alley-clue). No single forward path visits both shop-pick and alley-clue. The only way is start > shop > shop-pick > gathering > 'gather-alley' > alley > alley-clue > gathering > drone-street (or the mirror order). That forces the reader to reread 'gathering' (draft lines 181-207, choices 'Ride back to Tam's shop' / 'Ride back to the dark alley') and, via the alley, pass a stop they may have seen. Endings 1 and 2 are only reachable this way. This is a route that goes back over pages already read to collect an item.

Continuity on short routes. ending-5 (line 433) says 'She walked back to Tam's shop. He gave her hot soup', and Tam says 'listen to the little voice'. A reader who went start > alley > gathering > lane never met Tam or had soup. The reader who skipped the alley never heard of Aunt Ila, yet ending-4 (line 413) says 'It was Aunt Ila' and 'the flood gate' with no setup. ending-3 (line 394) mentions Tam's shop shut, which is also unexplained on the alley route.

Validation brief check warns that 1 sentence exceeds the brief's 16-word limit (validation.r7.json brief.warnings). Likely the long sentences in dash-past line 253 ('A drone swung round, and its flash lit the whole street...') or ending-1 line 356. Literacy reviewer should confirm.

lockedHint on 'pick-the-lock' (line 286) tells the reader what is needed but not where to find it. With the backtracking problem above, a reader who locked out has no pointer to the shop or alley. Consider hinting at the places. Fair, but weak.

Skills practised: Reading this story practises decoding closed-syllable words (bag, lock, pick, dash), sh words (shop, shade, flash) and ch words (chip, chain, chill) in running text, plus -ing endings (blinking, pounding, watching). The reader sequences events (the gathering passage and Nine's 'first the gate, then the track, then the far light'), infers who to trust from clues (the flood stamp, the grey mask) and works out meaning of words such as broker, drone and courier from context and the glossary. Choices and endings reward checking evidence before acting, which supports comprehension and inference.

Word sets meet their minimums on every route: closed-syllable-words 41/10, sh-words 27/8, ch-words 26/8 (literacy.r7). Every listed word appears in the draft. Each word-set word carries its declared pattern by spelling: cab/bag/pick/lock/mask/sack/dash/hack are closed syllables; shop/shade/shot/shut/flash/shell begin or end with sh; chip/chase/chill/much/lunch/chain all contain ch. 'patch' (tch) was correctly removed in r7.

The r7 revision notes call this a 'brief change' made while revising. Please regenerate or update the plan so the plan, brief and draft agree, and have the orchestrator or parent confirm the brief change. The weave comparison passes only because it counts set totals.

'chill' reads as forced. In 'start', 'a chill sat on the handlebars' is an odd image. In 'dash-past', 'A chill ran over the handlebars, but her tyre held' is a non sequitur, because a chill has no link to the tyre, and a reader may stumble on the meaning. Suggest a natural use such as 'The rain was cold and she felt a chill' to narrative-designer.

Several set words appear only once in the story text, on one branch only: 'lunch' and 'sack' (shop), 'chase' (drone-street), 'much' (shop-pick), 'shot' (drone-street). The set totals pass, but these words get little repetition. The plan wanted two or more placements per word. Consider a second natural use of each, for example 'lunch' or 'much' at Tam's or in an ending, so the reader meets them again.

'tyre' (dash-past) has an irregular, British spelling and is not a decodable word, though the rest of the story uses it consistently ('grey', 'tyre'). It is the only odd spelling in an otherwise regular passage. Consider 'wheel' or 'tire' for a dyslexic reader, or keep it and accept it as a tricky word.

Optional rereading on the alley-first route. A reader who goes start > alley > alley-clue > gathering has the stamp but not the pick set. Getting the pick means gathering > shop > shop-pick > alley > alley-clue > gathering, which rereads the alley (lines 136-180). This is not required: endings 1 and 2 are reachable forward with no repeat via start > shop > shop-pick > alley > alley-clue > gathering > drone-street > (hide-shade or dash-past) > threshold > pick-the-lock (lines 281-286, hint names both places). The earlier major (r7) is fixed. Reported as minor because the reread is only for a second read.

Gathering choices name places some readers have not seen. 'Ride back to Tam's shop' (line 193) shows for a reader who took start > alley and never met Tam. 'Ride back to the dark alley' (line 198) shows for a reader who took shop > leave-shop and never saw the alley. Consider neutral labels such as 'Ride to Tam's shop' and 'Ride to the dark alley'.

Small plot gap. At threshold (lines 270-274) the gate is shut and Mara picks the lock, then closes the gate behind her (line 305). Vex then 'stepped out of the fog' halfway across the bridge (line 307) with no explanation of how he got past the gate. Cab engine behind her (line 273) suggests he followed, so a line about a side path or his own key would fix it.

Validation report brief.warnings (validation.r8.json line 530) says 1 sentence exceeds the 16-word limit, but literacy.longSentences is empty (line 455) and I could not find it by hand count. The longest I counted is 16 words (ending-5, line 433, 'He gave her hot soup, some lunch from his sack and a seat by the fire.'). Literacy reviewer should locate it.
